newsitem.title: UK: London precious metals ponder next move.
newsitem.headline: London precious metals ponder next move.

text.p: Gold was steady and calm in early European trading following a period of sharp gains earlier this week, dealers said.
"The market is quiet and consolidating, although it opened firmer today than its close on Wednesday," a dealer said.
Bullion fixed at $383.70 an ounce, compared to $383.50 on Wednesday afternoon and a London close of $383.30/$383.80.
Prices have shot up from around $380 an ounce since Monday morning in a rally dealers attributed primarily to U.S-based investment funds covering short positions.
But so far gold has failed to muster enough momentum to convincingly breach stiff resistance around the technically signficant $384 an ounce level.
"We have to wait to see what New York does. If it closes on Friday in New York above $384, we might see $388-$390 next week," a dealer said.
But some dealers said gold was unlikely to move out of a $380-$385 price range until after the end-of-month expiry of over the counter options.
Options provide the right but not the obligation to buy or sell metal at a given price.
Price charts suggested that unless gold pushed past $386 is was destined to erode to pre-rally levels, whose nadir was the lowest in 18-months, some technical analysts said.
Silver, which has lagged behind gold in gains this week, was also facing difficulties surmounting its psychological $5.00 an ounce level.
It was indicated at $4.98/$5.00 an ounce, up one cent from Wednesday's London close.
But a breach of $5.00 would easily take prices to the important $5.08 resistance level, dealers said.
Platinum, buoyed by gold's gains, continued to make steady daily progress and was up $387.50/$388.50 an ounce, up $1.00.
Palladium was barely changed, down $0.15 at $118.00/$119.00, but also up more than $2.00 since the start of the week.
Recent political uncertainties in Russia, a key producer of platinum and palladium, were helping boost prices, dealers said.
